locator: I q.2 a.3 ad 1: ad infinitam Dei bonitatem pertinet, ut esse permittat mala, et ex eis eliciat bona
interpretation: God would in no way allow evil in his works unless he could bring good even out of evil; it belongs to his infinite goodness to permit evils and draw goods from them. Read per evil (every evil there is is one God draws good from). A weaker reading, on which God draws good from the evils taken together, is also defensible; the per-evil reading is the stronger commitment, so the consistency result proved with it holds for the weaker one too. The reading does not say what the good is or that it outweighs the evil.
